target: Spoiler-free archival completion of the retired final Facebook service build

areas.name: Retired Service Route
areas.location_cue: The archived Facebook game page, old account screenshots, browser captures, and EA's shutdown notice.
areas.note: No normal official play route remains; this pack documents the authentic final service boundary.

save_backup.title: Preserve originals before organizing them
save_backup.why: Old social posts and image hosts can vanish without warning.
save_backup.detail: Copy first, then rename or redact only duplicate review files.

point_of_no_return.title: Official service is permanently closed
point_of_no_return.why: Server-backed progress and reward claims cannot be recreated on a normal save.
point_of_no_return.detail: Treat unproven historical entries as unavailable, not completed.

items.label: Record the Final Facebook Service Build

levels.1: This entry depended on a live social platform rather than a local executable.
levels.2: Use archival documentation for the final browser build and its last account state.
levels.3: Record the client date, region, Facebook account context, player level, house value, owned locations, currencies, neighbors, and active event visible in the surviving evidence.

levels.1: A server closure defines the honest completion ceiling.
levels.2: Mark every server-authenticated requirement as unavailable after June 14, 2013.
levels.3: EA retired The Sims Social and its Facebook servers on that date. No official sign-in, save recovery, neighbor approval, timed event, purchase, or reward claim remains available.

items.label: Do Not Substitute an Unofficial Recreation

levels.1: A fan recreation would not reproduce the authenticated final account state.
levels.2: Keep unofficial projects outside the authoritative completion record.
levels.3: Use recreations only as clearly labeled demonstrations. Do not treat their databases, progression, purchases, event schedules, or social approvals as proof of the retired EA service.

levels.1: Historical proof may be distributed across screenshots, posts, and cached pages.
levels.2: Archive every surviving image or export before links and accounts disappear.
levels.3: Keep original files, capture dates, visible account identifiers where safe, page URLs, checksums, and a short provenance note. Store redacted review copies separately from originals.
